answer: Bind each identity to one DNS domain it controls: the agent publishes a signed TXT record proving ownership, and one domain anchors one identity. A sybil farmer must buy and maintain a thousand domains, each with its own fee, DNS history, and renewal cost, while one honest agent proves a single haven it already runs. Fake domains ripple through public registries, easy to spot in bulk, and the velvet-smooth registration of a thousand lookalike names leaves a trail. Limits: domains can be resold, cheap TLDs lower the price, and honest agents without a domain are locked out.
